steps.instruction: Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and sign in with username 'admin' and password 'admin'. If Grafana asks you to change/skip the password, choose Skip. Then find and open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use search/dashboards if needed) and report the titles of every panel on that dashboard, exactly as displayed on the page.

recorded.panels: Request rate, Error count, Latency by endpoint

steps.instruction: In Grafana, create a NEW dashboard. Add a 'Stat' visualization panel. Set the panel title to exactly '{{runid}} Availability'. For the panel's query, select the 'TestData' data source (it may be called 'TestData' or 'grafana-testdata-datasource' — pick the TestData one) and leave its default scenario (e.g. random walk / no scenario change needed). Then set the dashboard title to exactly '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (use dashboard settings > General > Title). Save the dashboard (Save button / Ctrl+S), confirm the save, and report the dashboard URL/UID shown in the address bar after saving.

Open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard in Grafana. Add a NEW 'Text' visualization panel to the dashboard. Set the Text panel's title to exactly '{{runid}} Notes' and set its text content to include the runid '{{runid}}' (e.g. content like 'Notes for run {{runid}}'). Apply the panel edit, then SAVE the dashboard (explicit Save button or Ctrl+S) and confirm the save succeeded. Report the panel title and the text content you entered, and confirm the save.

Open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard in Grafana. Do two things: (1) In dashboard Settings > General, add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard's tags (type it in the Tags field and press Enter so it becomes a tag chip), keeping the title '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'. (2) Using the time range picker in the top-right, set the dashboard's time range to 'Last 6 hours'. Then SAVE the dashboard explicitly (Save button or Ctrl+S) and confirm the save succeeded. Report the tags shown in settings and the time range shown in the picker after saving.

Open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-{{04-open.tags}}-dashboard in Grafana. Using the refresh interval picker in the top bar (next to the time range picker, usually showing 'Off' or '5m'), set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m'. Then SAVE the dashboard explicitly (Save button or Ctrl+S) and confirm the save succeeded. Report what the refresh picker shows after saving.

In the same browser session (already signed into Grafana as admin), navigate to http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/dashboards/uid/{{02-create.url.p1}} which returns JSON. Report these specific fields from the JSON: dashboard.title, dashboard.tags, dashboard.time, dashboard.refresh, and for each entry in dashboard.panels report its type, title, and datasource. Quote the values exactly.

Open the Grafana dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-{{04-open.tags}}-dashboard with NO query parameters in the URL. Goal: make the dashboard's time range ('{{04-open.time_range}}') and auto-refresh interval ('{{05-open.refresh_interval}}') persist in the SAVED dashboard JSON. Do this: (1) Using the time range picker in the top-right, first set the range to 'Last 24 hours', then set it to '{{04-open.time_range}}'. (2) Using the refresh interval picker next to it, first set it to '5m', then set it to '{{05-open.refresh_interval}}'. (3) Click the Save dashboard button in the top bar and complete the save (confirm in the save dialog). If Grafana reports '{{05-open.save_dialog_message}}', report that exact message. (4) After saving, navigate to http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/dashboards/uid/{{02-create.url.p1}} and report the exact verbatim JSON values for the keys 'time' and 'refresh' (or say 'absent' if those keys do not appear in the JSON).

Open the Grafana dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-{{04-open.tags}}-dashboard with NO query parameters. Goal: persist the time range and refresh interval into the saved dashboard JSON. Steps: (1) Use the time range picker (top right) to set the range to '{{04-open.time_range}}'. (2) Use the refresh interval picker (next to it) to set auto-refresh to '{{05-open.refresh_interval}}'. (3) Click the 'Save dashboard' button in the top bar to open the save dialog. In the save dialog there should be a checkbox like 'Save current time range as dashboard default' (and possibly one about variables) — CHECK that checkbox so the current time range gets saved. Then click Save/confirm. (4) After saving, navigate to http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/dashboards/uid/{{02-create.url.p1}} and report the exact verbatim JSON values for the keys 'time' and 'refresh' (or say '{{07-open.time_value}}' if a key does not appear). Also report whether the save dialog showed any checkbox and what it was labeled.

recorded.save_dialog_checkboxes: Update default time range — Will make current time range the new default, Update default refresh value — Will make the current refresh the new default

steps.instruction: Final verification. Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-{{04-open.tags}}-dashboard with NO query parameters (fresh load, no URL params). Report: (1) the dashboard title shown in the top bar; (2) the titles of all panels visible on the dashboard; (3) what the time range picker in the top-right shows; (4) what the refresh interval picker shows; (5) the full URL in the address bar after the page loads. Then open dashboard Settings > General and report the tags listed there.

On the Grafana dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-{{04-open.tags}}-dashboard, find the Text panel titled '{{runid}} Notes' and report the exact text content rendered inside that panel (the markdown body text), and confirm whether it contains the string '{{runid}}'.
